result.content:
---
# babylon_anarchy_governor defaults
#
# Execution environment selection. This still reads the pre-migration schema:
# ansible_control_plane.secret named the controller credential, and the EE was
# derived from it. Nothing in this file changed.
babylon_anarchy_governor_control_plane_secret: "{{ ansible_control_plane.secret }}"
babylon_anarchy_governor_ee_name: "{{ babylon_anarchy_governor_control_plane_secret }}-ee"

babylon_anarchy_governor_job_timeout: 3600

answer:
Root cause: PR 19034 migrated the ansible control plane schema and left a consumer of the old one behind.

The job fails in `babylon_anarchy_governor : Select the execution environment` with `'dict object' has no attribute 'secret'`. The governor's `roles/babylon_anarchy_governor/defaults/main.yaml` still reads `ansible_control_plane.secret` and derives the EE name from it -- nothing in this file changed. PR 19034 (`Migrate ansible_control_plane to ansible_controllers list`, merged 18:29Z) replaced that schema with an `ansible_controllers` list plus `ansible_controller_select_mode`, so the field the governor resolves no longer exists and the EE cannot be selected. Every catalog item goes through the governor, which is why all of them failed at once rather than a subset.

The migration itself is not wrong. What broke is that a downstream consumer of the removed field was never updated alongside it.

The failing tests are a contributing factor, not the cause. The `pr-19034` test run was killed out of memory at 18:22Z and reported no result, so the required `schema-compat` check never reported and the merge was allowed through on review override seven minutes later. Had the check run, it should have caught the incompatibility -- but the memory exhaustion did not make `ansible_control_plane.secret` undefined; removing the field did.

Fix: revert PR 19034 or update the governor defaults to read the new `ansible_controllers` schema.
